As I slept on the couch, I must have somehow became conscious of the situation, because I remember specifically wanting to get up and go lock the door (the door was only maybe 5 feet away).

I consciously knew I was lying on the couch and I was aware of my position and the I was aware of the unlocked door. I felt like I had control of my mind, as though I was awake. I could not move my body, however. I wanted to get up and go to the door but my body wouldn't move. It quickly became me just trying to move my arm, or even wiggle my fingers, but nothing... I was unable to move even the tips of my fingers.

I remember this being really frustrating and kind of scary. I began to feel almost a sense of urgency, like I suspected someone was going to break in and I needed to get to lock that door but I couldn't move. I think this made me feel even more awake inside my mind. Like I was lying there completely conscious but completely disconnected from my physical body. I remember trying to squirm left and right, anything to provoke movement.

Strangely I don't remember how I came out of it. I think I may have slowly regained control, locked the door, and went to sleep in my bed. It's possible I just fell back asleep though. This event was several years ago and the part I remember most was what I have described above.

I don't remember when I first started getting sleep paralysis, probably when I was about 17-18 years old (10 years ago). I had no idea what it was.
When I first started getting it, it manifested as a sound inside my head. It usually came on a few minutes after dozing off, I would sort of wake up a little bit but I was unable to move, the more I struggled or tried to move, the louder the sound in my head got.
It would get so bad that I thought my head was going to explode, and then, an instant later it would all be over. This would happen 2-3 times a week. Another time I remember "knowing" that there was someone (read something) sitting on the top of my wardrobe watching me, that was scary.

As time went on, the sound in my head gave way to hallucinations. When it came on I tried to yell, this never worked, or I would bang on the wall to get someone to come and wake me, often I would believe that this was successful, I could hear my fist banging or sometimes I believed I had successfully reached the light switch, I could see the light turn on in my room. I vividly remember one occurrence where I managed to roll out of bed and crawl to the door where I banged as hard as I could to wake my parents sleeping in the room above mine. I was wearing a white t shirt which was soaking wet with blood from my nose. My parents both came down and I was crying, asking them to wake me up, they were telling my I was awake and that I was being stupid, then an instant late, I actually do wake up, I'm lying alone, in the dark, in my bed.
Another time I remember, lying in bed, unable to move and someone was lying on top of me, he was whispering in my ear but I don't remember what.
I've had a skeleton try to choke me, when I came to I could still feel where the bony hands had been gripping my neck.
By far, the worst, which I've never told anyone about, was the time I thought I was being raped, when I did wake up and I realised what had happened I lay there crying for a while. That was the moment I truly discovered what a slave to my mind I was. I felt the same way I imagin an actual rape victim felt but that it was, at the same time, extremely disingenuous because it was "all in my head". All of the things that had previously happened to me over the years I was able to reconcile as manifestations in my mind and I wrote them off as such, I don't believe in anything supernatural which at times was counter-intuitive given my personal experiences but the feeling of being raped and knowing it was my own mind that was doing it to me was particularly taxing. One of my grandparents has developed schizophrenia and I know that is hereditary. I consider myself fairly intelligent but I'm terrified that one day my own mind will be actively trying to work against me by trying to convince me of the existence of unreal things.

I've read that attempting to move some of the minor muscles in your body can help to end an episode, flick your tongue, wiggle your fingers and toes, though I've not had much success with this.

Currently I experience SP about once or twice a week, very rarely is it a positive experience. For me, letting go and riding the experience has had mixed results. Sometimes it will turn into an interesting "lucid dream" other times it will simply be a few minutes of being unable to move. I don't see or feel presences any more, so I've got that going for me, which is nice.
